authority: OWNER 2026-10-26: 'I do not have those numbers. Use published figures and record them as assumptions.' Covers release-tree S81.XDIE (PHY dimensions, PHY power, signal/PG bump contract).
status: ASSUMPTION (published). Nothing in this file is measured on OpenTallas silicon or on an OpenTallas PHY view.
node_rule: ASAP7 is treated as N7-class (A100/N7 comparator). Published N5 figures are scaled to N7 with the TSMC N5/N7 density ratios; package figures (bump pitch, module width) are package technology and are NOT node-scaled.

n5_to_n7_area.basis: mixed-signal SerDes (analog + DSP) between the SRAM-cell ratio 0.027/0.021 = 1.29 and the logic-density ratio 1.84
n5_to_n7_area.source: G. Yeap et al., '5nm CMOS Production Technology Platform ...', IEDM 2019, doi:10.1109/IEDM19573.2019.8993577 (1.84x logic density, 0.021 um2 SRAM vs N7 0.027 um2)

s81_link_class: board-level 112G PAM4 SerDes (LR, DAC 1.3-1.44 m / AEC 2.15-2.2 m, docs/RELEASE_RACK.md 2.3). The S81 die has NO UCIe link: one die + one HBM3E stack per package. UCIe rows below are recorded for completeness (Qwen package-mate links use them) and are not checked against S81.

entries.unit: Gb/s per lane (PAM4, 56 GBd)
entries.source: OIF CEI-112G / IEEE 802.3ck lane class; https://www.oiforum.com/wp-content/uploads/00311c-OIF-112G-OFC-slides_ofc20_presentation.pdf
entries.scaling: none; 112G LR demonstrated at 7 nm (ISSCC 2020 6.2, ISSCC 2021 8.7)
entries.plan_value: 112 G x 6 lanes per ot_pdie_serdes macro (6 lanes is MODEL, RELEASE_RACK open item 3)

entries.unit: payload / raw
entries.source: RS(544,514) KP4 FEC (514/544) x 256b/257b transcoding, IEEE 802.3 100 Gb/s-per-lane PHYs (configs/hardware/technology.json links.rom_board_serdes)

entries.unit: mm2 per TX+RX lane (quad incl. PLL/DSP share)
entries.source: 'A 1-to-112Gb/s DSP-Based Wireline Transceiver with a Flexible Clocking Scheme in 5nm FinFET', VLSI 2022, doi:10.1109/VLSITechnologyandCir46769.2022.9830304: 'the quad transceiver occupies 1806x825um2'

entries.unit: mm2 per TX+RX lane
entries.source: SER.LANE_AREA_N5 x scaling.n5_to_n7_area
entries.plan_value: 0.40 mm2/lane (pg_domains.py PHY_AREA_MM2 = 2.4 for 6 lanes; quoted as 'published 7-nm' from the HBM B2m IR README; it is close to the N5 measurement, not an N7 figure)

entries.unit: mm2 per 6-lane macro
entries.source: 6 x SER.LANE_AREA_N7

entries.unit: um of die edge per lane (one lane row)
entries.source: VLSI 2022 quad 1806 um long side / 4 lanes = 451.5 um (N5), x n5_to_n7_linear
entries.plan_value: basis string 'shoreline 104 um' (that is the seal-ring offset, not a PHY shoreline)

entries.unit: um macro depth (one lane row)
entries.source: VLSI 2022 quad 825 um short side x n5_to_n7_linear

entries.unit: um shoreline for 6 lanes in one row
entries.source: 6 x SER.SHORE_PER_LANE_N7; a 2 x 3 fold halves shoreline (~1.66 mm) at ~2.0 mm depth

entries.unit: pJ/b per lane incl. analog + DSP, excl. FEC
entries.source: 5.6 pJ/b 5 nm incl. DSP (VLSI 2022, above); 7 nm analog 602 mW/ch excl. DSP = 5.4 pJ/b (JSSC 2021 doi:10.1109/JSSC.2020.3024261); low end 460 mW at 112 Gb/s = 4.1 pJ/b, 7 nm, 38 dB (ISSCC 2020 6.2, doi:10.1109/ISSCC19947.2020.9062925). Same value as configs/hardware/technology.json energy.link_j_per_bit.board_serdes_112g
entries.scaling: N7 LR with DSP (5 nm figure scaled up; 7 nm analog-only + DSP)

entries.unit: pJ/b (40 nm, upper bound; less at N7)
entries.source: RS(528,514) '90 mW', IEEE P802.3bj gustlin_01_0312 slide 6 (via technology.json note)

entries.unit: W per 6-lane macro, link active
entries.source: 6 x 112 Gb/s x SER.ENERGY (TX+RX per lane; FEC excluded)
entries.plan_value: IR trial 0.15 W/mm2 -> 0.205-0.236 W per window (results/die_trial_1024/codex_phy_1025, 'actual PHY power not yet supplied'); RELEASE_RACK charges 4.37 W/macro

entries.unit: W per ungated lane at 112 Gb/s
entries.source: technology.json board_serdes_112g note (static links: ungated = active)

entries.unit: signal bumps per 6-lane macro
entries.source: 4 per lane (TXP/TXN/RXP/RXN) + 2 refclk (differential); standard differential SerDes pinout

entries.unit: min. ground bumps per high-speed signal bump
entries.source: ASSUMPTION from industry practice (each 112G pair needs its own ground return/shield in the bump field); the nearest published bump map is UCIe-S (Das Sharma et al., IEEE TCPMT 12(9) 2022, doi:10.1109/TCPMT.2022.3207195, Fig. 7: 'good ground isolations ... to meet 32 GT/s'); derived PG share of a UCIe-S x16 module ~45% (see UCIE.S.PG_SHARE). No primary 112G bump map found.

entries.unit: um
entries.source: UCIe-S bump pitch 100-130 um (UCIe Hot Chips 2023 tutorial, Electrical Summary; Das Sharma TCPMT 2022: 'the minimal pitch of C4 bumps has reduced to about 100 um')
entries.plan_value: 150 um SerDes signal sites + 150-um core lattice C4 (conservative end)

entries.unit: um (2.5D micro-bump)
entries.source: UCIe-A 25-55 um (UCIe Hot Chips 2023 tutorial; UCIe SNIA SDC 2024 KPI table); HBM-PHY micro-bump 48 x 55 um (Alphawave Semi, 'Innovative Interposer Solutions for HBM3/4', DesignCon 2025)
entries.plan_value: 45 um VDDPHY/VSS rows (labelled 'C4' in die.pg.domains); 55 um HBM PHY

entries.unit: um of shoreline per 96 I/O (HBM3, Si interposer)
entries.source: Alphawave Semi, DesignCon 2025 (above): 'the 378um shoreline width constraint for fanning out 96 I/O ports in HBM3'
entries.plan_value: HBM PHY macro 8657 um shoreline for ~1,900 signals (1,900 / 96 x 378 um = 7.48 mm): fits

entries.unit: um width (shoreline) x depth, x64 module at 45-um pitch
entries.source: UCIe Consortium, Hot Chips 2023 tutorial 'Electrical Form Factor and Compliance', Electrical Summary (PHY dimension width 388.8, depth 1043 um at 45 um); Das Sharma et al. TCPMT 2022: 'The module width is fixed at 388.8 um ... At 45-um pitch, the bump field depth is about 1 mm'

entries.unit: um width x depth, x16 module (1540 um depth at 24/32 GT/s)
entries.source: UCIe Hot Chips 2023 Electrical Summary; Das Sharma TCPMT 2022 ('width of the block is chosen to be 571.5 um')

entries.unit: GT/s per lane (UCIe 1.1/2.0); 48/64 added in 3.0
entries.source: UCIe SNIA SDC 2024 (Das Sharma) KPI table; UCIe Hot Chips 2023

entries.unit: GB/s/mm
entries.source: UCIe SNIA SDC 2024 KPI table; Hot Chips 2023 Electrical Summary

entries.unit: pJ/b (rate-dependent targets; A 0.3-0.6 at 16-32 GT/s; S 0.75-1.25 at 24/32)
entries.source: UCIe Hot Chips 2023 Electrical Summary; idle 15% of peak
entries.scaling: spec target, node-independent; not used by S81

entries.unit: fraction of bump field that is power/ground (derived)
entries.source: derived from Das Sharma TCPMT 2022: ~400 IO/mm2 at 45 um pitch, hexagonal 45-um field = 1/(0.045^2 x 0.866) = 570 bumps/mm2 -> (570-400)/570 = 0.30

entries.unit: fraction of bump field that is power/ground (derived)
entries.source: derived: x16 module 571.5 x 1320 um at 110 um hexagonal = ~72 bumps; 40 signals (20 TX + 20 RX per TCPMT 2022 'basic UCIe-S block ... 20 signals') -> 32 PG = 0.45

entries.unit: Gb/s per signal pair, 12 links x 4 pairs/dir, 600 GB/s total, N7
entries.source: NVIDIA, 'NVIDIA Ampere Architecture In-Depth', https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-ampere-architecture-in-depth ; Hot Chips 2020 Choquette slides
entries.scaling: node anchor only: the A100 (N7) ran 50G NRZ off-package; 112G PAM4 at N7 is the ISSCC 2020/2021 class above, so the S81 lane rate is N7-consistent but beyond the A100's own off-chip rate

pg_c4_current_note: 4.37 W at 0.7 V = 6.2 A per macro on VDDPHY; dedicated VDDPHY bumps per window (IR trial) 270-320 -> ~20-23 mA per bump: well inside any published micro-bump EM limit (order 100 mA), no source pinned, not a check
